hints: Look carefully at where the blood in each side of the heart is heading. Does the left side really send blood to the pulmonary circulation?
Remember which ventricle has the bigger job: pumping a short distance to the lungs, or pumping all around the body. Which vessel should have the higher pressure?
walkthrough:
**Sort out the right side and left side**

Think of the heart as two pumps side by side. The right side collects deoxygenated blood from the body and sends it a short distance to the lungs. So statement 1 is correct.

The left side collects oxygenated blood from the lungs and sends it to the rest of the body, which is the systemic circulation, not the pulmonary circulation. So statement 2 is incorrect.

**Compare the ventricle walls and pressures**

The left ventricle has to push blood all around the body, a much longer distance and higher resistance than the short trip to the lungs. That is why its muscle wall is much thicker and it generates higher pressure. So statement 3 is correct.

**Compare aorta and pulmonary artery pressure**

Because the left ventricle is the stronger pump, pressure in the aorta is much higher than pressure in the pulmonary artery from the right ventricle. Statement 4 says the opposite, so statement 4 is incorrect.

Correct statements are 1 and 3 only, which is option B.

options.A: Includes 1 and 3 which are correct, but also includes 4 which is wrong because aortic pressure is higher, not lower, than pulmonary artery pressure.
options.B: Correctly selects 1 and 3 only. Right side carries deoxygenated blood to lungs, and left ventricle is thicker and higher pressure.
options.C: Wrong because it includes 2 and 4. Statement 2 is wrong (left side goes to systemic, not pulmonary) and 4 is wrong (aorta pressure is higher).
options.D: Wrong because both 2 and 4 are incorrect statements about circulation route and relative pressures.
